summary: Contract scope and renderer-only architecture are bounded and accurately distinguish artifact comparisons from browser evidence. Amend failure phases: focus capture occurs before teardown and can reject while the old renderer remains active; only failures after old unmount is attempted fail closed without rollback. Also require restoreFocus to return a boolean; current runtime accepts undefined as success, a pre-repair behavior assigned to N1.

observations.focus_capture_throws_before_teardown: replacement rejected; old unmount count 0; runtime failure null; snapshot remains available
observations.declared_and_bound_async_methods: rejected before teardown; old unmount count 0
observations.restore_focus_undefined: replacement committed and diagnostics recorded focusRestored true

prior_failure_history.history: An earlier reentrancy probe had 22 passed/1 failed; the test injection was scoped to the first replacement update, and the focused rerun passed 23/23.
The expected pre-implementation red run failed because frontend/dom/renderer.mjs did not exist; focused DOM and React regressions subsequently passed.
An overstrict raw bundle equality check failed because generated source-label comments included different temporary roots; the unsafe normalization approach was dropped and raw hashes retained.

limits: The five semantic tests use stub compiled symbols and mock renderers; they do not establish real four-app browser conformance.
The normalization vectors are passive fixtures. No bundle normalizer or proof based on normalized bundle equality was used.
No hostile Proxy or side-effecting-getter security guarantee is claimed; the contract bounds renderers as trusted structural adapters.
The integrated four-app/five-fixture browser matrix is separate N3 evidence and was not part of this review.
